A letter, before the first move

Dear Archit,

At 22, you still play life the way you play chess: patiently, thoughtfully, always a few moves ahead. You think before you speak and calculate before you leap, and somehow you still surprise me every single time.

Thank you for being the calm in my loudest moments, and the person I most want to sit across the board from, even when you’re quietly winning. You bring the logic when I bring the feelings, and somewhere behind that serious face is the softest heart I know.

I know exactly how to make you smile: a well-timed checkmate, anything green, a 5 Star you pretend you won’t share, and a hot plate of South Indian food.

So this year, may every move be a brilliant one, every square a little greener, and every day as sweet as that chocolate. Whatever the position, I’m on your side of the board.

Happy birthday, my king.
Your queen (Harshda) ♛

A proof, for the logical one

Because feelings are better with a little rigour.

Theorem. Archit at 22 is better than Archit at 21.

Proof (by induction). Base case: every year so far, you improved. Inductive step: assume you were great at age n. At n+1 you have one more year of wisdom, one more year of patience, and one more year of my love. So you are greater still.

Hence proved, and then some. ∎
